rules.title: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (AB 1482) – Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are capped at 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, measured against the lowest rent in the prior 12 months. Local rent control that is stricter supersedes this cap.
rules.key_value: lesser of 5% + CPI or 10% per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing issued a certificate of occupancy more than 15 years before the increase (rolling); not deed-restricted affordable; not covered by stricter local rent control
rules.exemptions: Housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control (Civ. Code § 1947.12(d)(3)); separately alienable single-family homes/condos not owned by a REIT, corporation or corporate-member LLC where notice given; owner-occupied duplexes
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction – Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may not end the tenancy without a stated at-fault or no-fault just cause; no-fault terminations require one month of relocation assistance or rent waiver.
rules.key_value: just cause required after 12 months of occupancy; 1 month relocation assistance for no-fault
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancy months: 12; Housing issued a certificate of occupancy more than 15 years ago; not subject to a more protective local just-cause ordinance
rules.exemptions: COO within previous 15 years; transient hotels; care facilities; dormitories; owner-shared units; owner-occupied SFR renting ≤2 units/bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex; separately alienable SFR/condo not owned by REIT/corporation/corporate LLC with notice; deed-restricted affordable housing; property subject to a local just-cause ordinance adopted on/before 2019-09-01 or a more protective later one (§ 1946.2(i))
rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy

rules.title: Security deposit cap (AB 12) – Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5(c)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit exceeding one month's rent (in addition to first month's rent). A small landlord who is a natural person (or all-natural-person LLC) owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total may charge up to two months' rent.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies; 2-month exception only if landlord is a natural person/natural-person LLC owning ≤2 rental properties with ≤4 dwelling units total
rules.exemptions: Small-landlord two-month exception (Civ. Code § 1950.5(c)(5)); exception unavailable where prospective tenant is a service member; not applicable to security collected before 2024-07-01
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy

rules.title: Application screening fee cap – Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6
rules.requirement: An application screening fee may not exceed the landlord's actual out-of-pocket screening costs and in no case more than $30 per applicant (1997 base), which may be adjusted annually for CPI since 1998-01-01; a receipt and refund of unused amounts are required.
rules.key_value: $30 (1997 base) adjusted annually by CPI from 1998-01-01; no single official 2026 dollar figure
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental applications
rules.exemptions: Fee may not be charged when no unit is available; reusable screening reports (§ 1950.1)
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
rules.conflict_note: Organisers' README: the CA screening-fee cap has no single official 2026 dollar figure. Berkeley Rent Board publishes $68.96 for 2026 (D005); other calculators differ. Key value recorded as statutory formula, not a dollar figure.

rules.title: FEHA source-of-income protection (incl. Section 8 vouchers) – Cal. Gov. Code § 12955
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not discriminate against applicants or tenants because of source of income, which includes federal, state or local housing subsidies such as Section 8 Housing Choice Vouchers paid to the landlord on the tenant's behalf.
rules.key_value: source of income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) is a protected characteristic
rules.coverage_conditions: All housing accommodations covered by FEHA
rules.quoted_span: federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including, but not limited to, federal housing assistance vouchers issued under Section 8 of the United States Housing Act of 1937 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 1437f)

rules.title: Common pricing algorithm prohibition (AB 325, Cartwright Act) – Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software using competitor data to recommend or set prices) as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade, or to coerce another person to adopt a price it recommends. Applies to residential rent-setting software statewide.
rules.key_value: prohibition on use/distribution of common pricing algorithms in restraint of trade
rules.coverage_conditions: All persons (landlords and vendors) in California; not limited to housing
rules.exemptions: End consumers are not "persons" (§ 16729(d)(5))
rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (added by AB 325, Stats. 2025 ch. 338)
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

rules.title: No rent increase limits rule at state level
rules.requirement: New Jersey has no statewide rent cap; rent control is delegated to municipalities (Jersey City ch. 260, Hoboken ch. 155, Newark Title XIX). State law only bars "unconscionable" increases as an eviction defence (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(f)).
rules.quoted_span: provided the increase in rent is not unconscionable and complies with any and all other laws or municipal ordinances governing rent increases

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act – N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1
rules.requirement: A residential tenant may be removed only on one of the statutory good-cause grounds (e.g., non-payment, disorderly conduct, breach, owner occupancy of a building of three units or fewer); lease expiry alone is not a ground.
rules.key_value: statutory good cause required for removal
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental premises except owner-occupied buildings with not more than two rental units and transient hotel/guest-house occupancy
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units; hotels/motels/guest houses rented to transients or seasonal tenants
rules.quoted_span: other than (1) owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units or a hotel, motel or other guest house or part thereof rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant

rules.title: Rent Security Deposit Act cap – N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2
rules.requirement: A landlord may not require a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent; annual additional security may not exceed 10% of the current deposit.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental dwelling premises; owner-occupied premises with ≤2 rental units are excluded unless the tenant gives 30 days' written notice invoking the Act (N.J.S.A. 46:8-26)
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units where the tenant has not invoked the Act (N.J.S.A. 46:8-26); seasonal rentals under 125 days
rules.quoted_span: An owner or lessee may not require more than a sum equal to 1 1/2 times 1 month's rental according to the terms of contract, lease, or agreement as a security for the use or rental of real property used for dwelling purposes.

rules.title: Residential rental application fee cap ($50) – P.L.2025, c.405 (N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1)
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge an application or similar fee exceeding $50 to apply to lease a residential rental property; the cap is CPI-adjusted each January from the year after enactment.
rules.key_value: $50 (CPI-adjusted from January 2027)
rules.coverage_conditions: Minimum units: 3; Residential rental property other than units in one- or two-family dwellings
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in a one-family or two-family dwelling; NJ Real Estate Commission licensees who are not the landlord
rules.quoted_span:
shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act (criminal-record screening) – P.L.2021, c.110 (N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 et seq.)
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not ask about an applicant's criminal record before making a conditional offer, may never consider certain records, and may withdraw an offer only after an individualised assessment with written notice and a chance to respond.
rules.key_value: no criminal-record inquiry before conditional offer; individualised assessment required
rules.coverage_conditions: All housing providers; limited exceptions for owner-occupied small buildings (N.J.S.A. 46:8-54 definitions)
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex-offender registrants and methamphetamine production on federally assisted premises may be considered; owner-occupied premises with ≤4 units are excluded from "housing provider" (per Act definitions – not quoted here)
rules.quoted_span: regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.

rules.title: Law Against Discrimination – source of lawful income used for rent – N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to refuse to rent or otherwise discriminate in housing because of a person's source of lawful income used for rental payments (e.g., housing vouchers).
rules.key_value: source of lawful income (incl. vouchers) is a protected category
rules.coverage_conditions: All real property rentals subject to the LAD
rules.exemptions: LAD owner-occupied small-building exemptions (N.J.S.A. 10:5-5(n)) – not quoted here
rules.quoted_span: or source of lawful income used for rental or mortgage payments;

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act – P.L.2026, c.43
rules.requirement: From 2027-07-01, rental property owners may not pay for or use a "coordinator" (algorithmic revenue-management software processing competitors' nonpublic data), and coordinators may not facilitate parallel pricing coordination; violations are New Jersey Antitrust Act violations.
rules.key_value: ban on use of algorithmic rent-setting coordinators (effective 2027-07-01)
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential dwelling units in New Jersey
rules.exemptions: Spreadsheets without AI; databases that only query unprocessed data; public free rent estimates; brokerage databases that do not recommend prices; government affordability controls
rules.quoted_span:
This act shall take effect on the first day of
the twelfth month next following the date of enactment.
rules.conflict_note: Possible preemption of Jersey City and Hoboken algorithmic-pricing ordinances when the FAIR Act takes effect (P.L.2026 c.43 § 6(b)); organisers' README lists this as an open question. Not resolved here.

rules.title: No rent increase limits rule at state level
rules.requirement: State law bars local rent control: M.G.L. c.40P, § 4 ("No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind"); no statewide cap exists; the 2026 rent-control ballot initiative (IP 25-21) was struck by the SJC on 2026-06-23 (see MA-RENT-P1).
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind

rules.title: Rent-control ballot initiative IP 25-21 (struck by the SJC 2026-06-23)
rules.requirement: A proposed 2026 ballot question would have limited annual residential rent increases statewide; the Supreme Judicial Court ruled on 2026-06-23 that it could not go before voters because it related to religion. No rent cap results.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would have applied statewide if enacted; never in force
rules.citation: Initiative Petition 25-21 (Mass. 2026); Cella v. Attorney General (SJC, decided 2026-06-23)
rules.quoted_span: The state’s Supreme Judicial Court ruled a ballot question seeking to bring rent control back to Massachusetts cannot go forward this November, because it includes a religious exemption.

rules.title: No just cause eviction rule at state level
rules.requirement: Massachusetts has no statewide just-cause eviction requirement; tenancies at will may be ended by notice (M.G.L. c.186, § 12) and non-payment terminations need a 14-day notice to quit (c.186, §§ 11, 12, 31). Boston and Cambridge impose only notice-of-rights duties (see BOS-JUST-01, CAM-JUST-01).
rules.citation: M.G.L. c.186, §§ 11, 12 (notice to quit; no just-cause requirement)
rules.quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party

rules.title: Security deposit limit – M.G.L. c.186, § 15B(1)(b)
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy a landlord may require only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to the first month's rent, and the cost of a new lock and key; the deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing account.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (security deposit)
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies in Massachusetts
rules.quoted_span: a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)

rules.title: Prohibition on landlord application fees – M.G.L. c.186, § 15B(1)(b)
rules.requirement: Because a landlord may require only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit and a lock/key charge at or before the start of a tenancy, landlords may not charge rental application or screening fees. (Licensed brokers are regulated separately under 254 CMR 7 and M.G.L. c.112, § 87DDD½.)
rules.key_value: $0 – landlords may not charge application fees
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies in Massachusetts (lessors and their agents)
rules.exemptions: Licensed real estate brokers acting under their own contract with the tenant (M.G.L. c.112, § 87DDD½; 254 CMR 7)
rules.quoted_span: no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:

rules.title: Public-assistance / housing-subsidy discrimination ban – M.G.L. c.151B, § 4(10)
rules.requirement: A person furnishing rental accommodations may not discriminate against an applicant or tenant because they receive public assistance or federal, state or local housing subsidies (e.g., Section 8), or because of any requirement of such a program.
rules.key_value: recipients of public assistance / housing subsidies are protected
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental accommodations subject to c.151B (owner-occupied two-family exemptions in c.151B § 4(6)/(11) not quoted)
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two-family dwellings for certain provisions (M.G.L. c.151B, § 4(6)) – not quoted
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient, or because of any requirement of such public assistance, rental assistance, or housing subsidy program.

rules.title: S.2983 – An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting (pending)
rules.requirement: A pending Senate bill would prohibit algorithmic rent setting statewide; it was reported favourably by the Joint Committee on Housing on 2026-03-12 and referred to Senate Ways and Means. It is not law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would apply statewide (all MA addresses) if enacted
rules.quoted_span: Bill reported favorably by committee and referred to the committee on

rules.title: H.5222 – An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market (pending)
rules.requirement: A pending House bill (new draft of H.1564) would prevent algorithmic rent fixing statewide; reported favourably by the Joint Committee on Housing on 2026-03-12 and referred to House Ways and Means. It is not law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would apply statewide (all MA addresses) if enacted
rules.quoted_span: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market

rules.title: Broker fee reform – M.G.L. c.112, § 87DDD½ (as amended by St. 2025, c.9, § 43)
rules.requirement: A rental broker's fee may be charged only to the party (landlord or tenant) who engaged and contracted with the broker; a tenant who did not engage the broker cannot be made to pay the broker fee.
rules.key_value: broker fee payable only by the party who engaged the broker
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rentals in Massachusetts arranged through a licensed broker or salesperson
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: CORI in housing – 803 CMR 5.00 (Criminal Offender Record Information: housing)
rules.requirement: Housing providers that obtain Criminal Offender Record Information must follow DCJIS regulations limiting how CORI is requested, used and shared in housing decisions.
rules.key_value: regulated access to and use of CORI by housing providers
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers in Massachusetts that use CORI

rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance annual allowable increase – LAMC § 151.06
rules.requirement: For RSO units (generally buildings first built on or before 1978-10-01), rent may be raised once every 12 months by the published allowable percentage (3% for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30). Ordinance 188795 (effective 2026-02-02) changed the formula to 90% of CPI with a 1% floor and 4% cap from 2026-07-01 and removed the utility and dependent surcharges.
rules.key_value: 3% (Jul 2025–Jun 2026); from Jul 2026 formula = 90% of CPI, floor 1%, cap 4%
rules.coverage_conditions: Certificate of occupancy on/before: 1978-10-01; Minimum units: 2; Rental units with a certificate of occupancy on or before 1978-10-01 (apartments, duplexes, 2+ SFDs on one parcel, condos/townhomes with pre-1996 tenancies, ADUs, mobile homes); replacement units under § 151.28
rules.exemptions: Units first built after 1978-10-01 (unless replacement units); single-family dwellings (one per parcel); luxury exemption; government-owned/subsidised units (partial)
rules.citation: L.A. Mun. Code § 151.06 (as amended by Ord. No. 188795)
rules.quoted_span: Generally, the RSO applies to rental properties that were first built on or before October 1, 1978, as well as replacement units under
rules.conflict_note: Organisers' README: LA RSO new formula has two published effective dates — 2026-02-02 (LAHD) vs 2026-01-24 (Apartment Association of Greater Los Angeles). City Clerk council file 23-1134 records Ord. 188795 "Ordinance effective date: February 2, 2026" (checked 2026-10-03). Not resolved unilaterally; primary evidence favours 2026-02-02.

rules.title: Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO) – LAMC § 165.03 (Ord. No. 187737)
rules.requirement: For residential units in Los Angeles not covered by the RSO, a landlord may not end a tenancy without one of the listed at-fault or no-fault just causes once the tenant has lived in the unit for six months or the initial lease has expired; no-fault evictions require relocation assistance.
rules.key_value: just cause required after 6 months or lease expiry; relocation assistance for no-fault
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancy months: 6; Residential rental units in the City of Los Angeles not subject to the RSO, including single-family dwellings and post-1978 buildings
rules.exemptions: RSO units (covered instead by LAMC 151.09); transient hotels; licensed care facilities; fraternity/sorority houses; owner's roommate; certain cooperatives, non-profit homeless facilities and HACLA/government-owned properties
rules.citation: L.A. Mun. Code § 165.03 (Art. 5.3, Ch. XVI; Ord. No. 187737)
rules.quoted_span: The JCO covers most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles that are not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

rules.title: RSO legal reasons for eviction and relocation assistance – LAMC § 151.09
rules.requirement: For RSO units, a landlord may evict only for the fourteen legal reasons listed in the RSO (at-fault and no-fault); no-fault evictions require relocation assistance and a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict filed with LAHD, and all termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days.
rules.key_value: RSO just-cause grounds + relocation assistance
rules.coverage_conditions: Certificate of occupancy on/before: 1978-10-01; Minimum units: 2; RSO rental units (certificate of occupancy on or before 1978-10-01)
rules.exemptions: Non-RSO units (covered by the JCO instead)
rules.quoted_span:
three (3) business days of service on the tenant
per Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5.

rules.title: Interest on security deposits for RSO units – LAMC § 151.06.02
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO units must pay tenants interest on security deposits, accruing monthly since 1990-11-01, paid or credited at least annually at the rate set by the city.
rules.key_value: annual interest on deposits (RSO units)
rules.coverage_conditions: Certificate of occupancy on/before: 1978-10-01; Minimum units: 2; RSO rental units
rules.exemptions: Non-RSO units
rules.quoted_span: Interest Payments on Security Deposits

rules.title: No application screening fees rule at city level
rules.requirement: No Los Angeles ordinance caps application screening fees; Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 (CA-FEE-01) governs.

rules.title: Source of income discrimination prohibition – LAMC § 45.67 (Art. 5.6, Ch. IV)
rules.requirement: Anyone renting or listing housing in Los Angeles may not refuse to rent, apply different terms, misrepresent availability or advertise a preference based on a person's source of income, including housing assistance payments such as Section 8.
rules.key_value: source of income (incl. housing vouchers) protected
rules.coverage_conditions: All housing accommodations offered for rent in the City of Los Angeles
rules.quoted_span: refuse to rent or lease, or to continue to rent or lease, a housing accommodation; refuse to enter into or renew a rental agreement, lease or housing assistance payment contract

rules.title: No algorithmic rent setting rule at city level
rules.requirement: As of 2026-10-01 the City of Los Angeles has not enacted an algorithmic rent-setting ban; the only corpus document is a 2024-09-03 Council motion (CF 24-1031) instructing LAHD to report on feasibility. State law (CA-ALG-01) governs LA addresses.
rules.citation: L.A. City Council motion CF 24-1031 (2024-09-03) – no ordinance
rules.quoted_span: report on the number of ownership and management entities that are using algorithm-based
rules.conflict_note: Absence of an LA ordinance inferred from the corpus and an Aug-2026 law-firm survey; not confirmed against the LAMC or council files.

rules.title: Rent Ordinance annual allowable increase – S.F. Admin. Code § 37.3
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units (generally buildings with a certificate of occupancy on or before 1979-06-13), the landlord may raise rent once a year by the Rent Board's annual allowable increase: 1.6% for 2026-03-01 to 2027-02-28.
rules.coverage_conditions: Certificate of occupancy on/before: 1979-06-13; Rental units with a certificate of occupancy on or before 1979-06-13 (Costa-Hawkins exempts separately alienable SFRs/condos from the rent limits)
rules.exemptions: Units first occupied/COO after 1979-06-13; single-family homes and condos with post-1995 tenancies (Costa-Hawkins); government-regulated rents
rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.

rules.title: Rent Ordinance just cause for eviction – S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a)
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of the 17 just causes listed in § 37.9(a); this applies even to newer units (post-1979 COO) that are exempt from the rent-increase limits.
rules.key_value: 17 enumerated just causes
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including post-1979 units exempt from rent limits
rules.exemptions: Units fully exempt from the Rent Ordinance (e.g., certain government-owned housing, some non-profit and institutional housing)
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.

rules.title: Interest on security deposits – S.F. Admin. Code ch. 49
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay tenants annual interest on security deposits held for a year or more at the rate set by the Rent Board: 4.2% for 2026-03-01 to 2027-02-28.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential units in San Francisco where a deposit has been held for at least one year
rules.quoted_span: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

rules.title: No application screening fees rule at city level
rules.requirement: No San Francisco ordinance caps application screening fees; Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 (CA-FEE-01) governs.

rules.title: Fair Chance Ordinance (housing) – S.F. Police Code art. 49
rules.requirement: Affordable-housing providers in San Francisco may not consider certain arrest or conviction history and must follow fair-chance procedures when screening applicants.
rules.key_value: criminal-history limits for affordable housing providers
rules.coverage_conditions: Affordable housing (city-funded or inclusionary) in San Francisco; not all private market-rate rentals
rules.exemptions: Market-rate housing not covered by the Fair Chance Ordinance's housing provisions
rules.citation: S.F. Police Code art. 49 (§§ 4901 et seq.)
rules.quoted_span: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.
rules.conflict_note: Coverage limited to affordable housing; whether a sample address is affordable housing is not in the data → expected result unknown. Category boundary (screening_restrictions) acceptable; coverage detail from general knowledge, not quoted.

rules.title: Prohibition on algorithmic devices to set rents – S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell or use an algorithmic device that analyses nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents or occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco; tenants and the City Attorney may sue.
rules.key_value: ban on sale/use of algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential units in San Francisco
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

rules.title: No rent increase limits rule at city level
rules.requirement: The City of San Diego has no local rent-increase cap; Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 (CA-RENT-01) governs San Diego addresses.
rules.quoted_span:
The rights conferred by 
this Division are in addition to any existing rights provided to tenants by state or 
federal law.

rules.title: Residential Tenant Protection Ordinance – SDMC § 98.0704
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without at-fault or no-fault just cause as listed in SDMC 98.0704; no-fault terminations require relocation assistance of two months' rent (three for elderly/disabled tenants).
rules.key_value: just cause required; 2 months relocation (3 for elderly/disabled)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in the City of San Diego other than the exemptions in § 98.0703 (incl. COO within previous 15 years)
rules.exemptions: Transient/short-term occupancy; deed-restricted affordable housing (not Section 8); mobilehomes; care facilities; dormitories; owner-shared units; owner-occupied SFR (≤2 bedrooms/ADUs rented); owner-occupied duplex; housing with COO within previous 15 years; separately alienable SFR/condo not owned by REIT/corporation/corporate LLC with notice
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.

rules.title: No security deposits rule at city level
rules.requirement: No San Diego ordinance regulates security deposits; Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 (CA-DEP-01) governs.

rules.title: No application screening fees rule at city level
rules.requirement: No San Diego ordinance caps application screening fees; Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 (CA-FEE-01) governs.

rules.title: Prohibition of discrimination based on a tenant's source of income – SDMC §§ 98.0801–98.0803
rules.requirement: Landlords in the City of San Diego may not refuse to rent, terminate, misrepresent availability or impose different terms based on a person's source of income, including housing vouchers, and must evaluate the applicant's entire source of income.
rules.key_value: source of income (incl. vouchers) protected
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in the City of San Diego

rules.title: Prohibition of anti-competitive automated rent price-fixing – SDMC § 98.1103
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or provide an algorithmic device (software analysing nonpublic competitor data of two or more landlords) to a landlord, or for a landlord to use one to set rents or occupancy levels for residential rental property in San Diego; tenants may sue for up to $1,000 per violation.
rules.key_value: ban on sale/use of algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental property in the City of San Diego
rules.exemptions: Reports from aggregated data more than 90 days old; affordable-housing rent-limit software; appraisal software

rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance annual general adjustment – BMC § 13.76.110
rules.requirement: For fully covered units (generally multifamily buildings built before 1980), rent ceilings may rise each January by the Annual General Adjustment of 65% of CPI, never above 5%: 1.0% for 2026.
rules.key_value: 1.0% for 2026 (65% of CPI; 5% cap)
rules.coverage_conditions: Certificate of occupancy on/before: 1980-06-30; Fully covered units: multifamily units with a certificate of occupancy on or before 1980-06-30 (new construction after June 1980 is only partially covered: no rent control)
rules.exemptions: New construction (COO after June 1980) – partially covered, no rent ceiling; single-family homes with tenancies from 1996 onward; most condominiums; golden duplexes; owner-shared units; ADUs with owner occupancy; nonprofit cooperatives; dormitories
rules.quoted_span:
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance – BMC § 13.76.130
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units may be evicted only for a just cause listed in the ordinance; Measure BB (2024) bars non-payment evictions for debt under one month of HUD Fair Market Rent and removed the failure-to-sign-a-new-lease ground.
rules.key_value: enumerated just causes; non-payment eviction only if debt ≥ 1 month FMR
rules.coverage_conditions: All units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance (including new construction and single-family homes)
rules.exemptions: Exempt units: golden duplex; owner-shared kitchen/bath where owner lived there first; owner-occupied ADU properties (tenancies after 2018-11-07); dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives
rules.quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).

rules.title: Interest on security deposits – Berkeley Rent Ordinance (BMC § 13.76.070)
rules.requirement: Landlords of units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the end of each year (prorated on move-out).
rules.key_value: annual interest on deposits (covered units)
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance
rules.exemptions: Exempt units (see BERK-JUST-01)
rules.quoted_span: landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

rules.title: Tenant screening fee disclosure and renewal-fee ban – BMC ch. 13.78
rules.requirement: An owner charging a screening fee must give the applicant a clear tenant-screening-fee rights statement and state the maximum fee permitted under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b) (BMC 13.78.010); non-refundable fees to existing tenants for renewals or roommate changes are prohibited (BMC 13.78.016).
rules.key_value: disclosure of state fee cap required; no non-refundable renewal/roommate fees
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Berkeley
rules.quoted_span: cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.conflict_note: Borderline categorisation: BMC 13.78 is a disclosure/notice duty plus a renewal-fee ban, not a fee cap. Alternative is a negative finding (BERK-FEE-00) with the state cap governing. Decision reserved for Hamza (open_questions.md).

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance – BMC ch. 13.106
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers in Berkeley may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions, with limited exceptions (lifetime sex-offender registrants, certain federally assisted housing, small owner-occupied properties).
rules.key_value: ban on criminal-history inquiry and use in housing decisions
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental housing providers in Berkeley
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex-offender registrants; public housing/Section 8 limited exemptions; owner-occupied properties of 1–3 units where an owner of record lives; owner move-back tenancies (BMC 13.76.130 A.9); existing tenants subletting/adding roommates
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

rules.title: Prohibition on coordinated pricing algorithms – BMC ch. 13.63 (Ord. 7992-NS)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell or provide to Berkeley landlords, or for a landlord to use, a coordinated pricing algorithm that uses nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels; each unit and month is a separate violation (up to $1,000 each).
rules.key_value: ban on sale/use of coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley
rules.exemptions: Aggregated anonymous reports; affordable-housing rent-limit tools; market research, appraisal and software testing uses
rules.quoted_span:
B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.
rules.conflict_note: Organisers' README: two published effective dates — 2026-03-01 (ordinance text) vs January 2026 (Aug-2026 law-firm alert). Verified history: Ord. 7956-NS added ch. 13.63 (adopted 2025-03-25, eff. 2025-04-24); Ord. 7974-NS (adopted 2025-07-08, eff. 2025-08-07) inserted "The provisions of this Chapter shall not take effect until March 1, 2026"; Ord. 7992-NS (adopted 2025-12-02, eff. 2026-01-01 per berkeley.municipal.codes) re-enacted the chapter without that clause. Decided by Hamza 2026-10-04 (Q1): effective_date 2026-01-01; conflict_flag retained (organisers' open question).

rules.title: Rent Control Ordinance – Jersey City Code ch. 260 (§ 260-3)
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled dwellings, a landlord may not raise rent at lease expiry by more than the lesser of 4% or the CPI change over the lease term; buildings of one to four units are exempt, as is new construction for the statutory exemption period.
rules.key_value: lesser of 4% or CPI
rules.coverage_conditions: Minimum units: 5; Rent-controlled dwellings as defined in § 260-1; properties with 1–4 units are exempt
rules.exemptions: 1–4 unit properties (per the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations); newly constructed multiple dwellings for the N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1 exemption period; owner-occupied and other § 260 exemptions (not quoted)
rules.quoted_span: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control

rules.title: No just cause eviction rule at city level
rules.requirement: Jersey City has no local just-cause ordinance; the state Anti-Eviction Act (NJ-JUST-01) governs.

rules.title: No security deposits rule at city level
rules.requirement: No Jersey City deposit ordinance; N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 (NJ-DEP-01) governs.

rules.title: No application screening fees rule at city level
rules.requirement: No Jersey City application-fee ordinance; N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1 (NJ-FEE-01) governs.

rules.title: No screening restrictions rule at city level
rules.requirement: No Jersey City screening-restriction ordinance identified; the NJ Fair Chance in Housing Act and LAD (NJ-SCRN-01/02) govern.

rules.title: Ban on algorithmic rent-setting using nonpublic competitor data – Jersey City Code § 218-12 (Ord. 25-057)
rules.requirement: Landlords in Jersey City may not use rent-setting software or algorithms that process nonpublic competitor information to set or recommend rents; single owners coordinating only their own properties and licensed real-estate agents are excluded.
rules.key_value: ban on landlord use of algorithmic rent-setting with nonpublic competitor data
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental properties in Jersey City
rules.exemptions: Pricing across multiple properties under a single owner; licensed real estate agents
rules.conflict_note: NJ FAIR Act may preempt this ordinance once effective (2027-07-01); organisers list this as an open question (README § 9) and require conflict flags on Jersey City addresses in T3. Effective date only at month precision (NJ ordinances take effect 20 days after final passage/publication; Morgan Lewis: "effective June 2025").

rules.title: Rent Control – Hoboken Code ch. 155 (§ 155-5)
rules.requirement: At lease expiry a Hoboken landlord may not raise rent by more than the lesser of 5% or the CPI change over the lease term; one increase per 12 months. Hotels, new construction (post-1987 multiple dwellings for the statutory exemption period) and a few other categories are exempt; there is no small-building or owner-occupancy exemption.
rules.key_value: lesser of 5% or CPI per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: All dwellings rented in Hoboken except § 155-2 exemptions (no unit-count or owner-occupancy exemption)
rules.exemptions: Motels/hotels; newly constructed dwellings on first rental (registered); industrial/commercial property; institutional student housing; government-owned housing; buildings vacant since 1984-01-01; multiple dwellings constructed after 1987-06-25 for the mortgage-amortisation/30-year period under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1 et seq.
rules.quoted_span: no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.

rules.title: No just cause eviction rule at city level
rules.requirement: Hoboken has no local just-cause ordinance; the state Anti-Eviction Act (NJ-JUST-01) governs.

rules.title: No security deposits rule at city level
rules.requirement: No Hoboken deposit ordinance; N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 (NJ-DEP-01) governs.

rules.title: No application screening fees rule at city level
rules.requirement: No Hoboken application-fee ordinance; N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1 (NJ-FEE-01) governs.

rules.title: No screening restrictions rule at city level
rules.requirement: No Hoboken screening-restriction ordinance identified; NJ Fair Chance in Housing Act and LAD govern.

rules.title: Prohibition on price fixing using algorithmic pricing – Hoboken Code ch. 158 (Ord. B-781)
rules.requirement: Landlords renting any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that analyse nonpublic competitor information (less than 365 days old) to coordinate, recommend or implement rents, lease terms or occupancy levels; penalties include fines up to $2,000 and community service.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic price fixing using nonpublic competitor information
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential dwelling units in Hoboken (primary residences)
rules.exemptions: Medical/long-term care and detention facilities; information more than 365 days old or publicly available at no cost
rules.citation: Hoboken Code ch. 158 (Ord. No. B-781, adopted 2025-07-09)
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.
rules.conflict_note: NJ FAIR Act may preempt this ordinance once effective (organisers' open question; T3 conflict flags for Hoboken addresses). Effective date at month precision: adopted 2025-07-09; NJ ordinances take effect ~20 days after final passage and publication; Morgan Lewis gives "effective July 2025".

rules.title: Disclosure duties for renewal rent increases above 10% – Hoboken Code ch. 158 (Ord. B-750)
rules.requirement: A Hoboken landlord seeking a renewal rent increase of more than 10% year over year must first give the tenant an itemisation of the costs behind the increase, a statement whether a rent algorithm was used, notice of the right to challenge an unconscionable increase, and the Division of Housing's contact details; fines up to $1,000 per incident.
rules.key_value: disclosures required for renewal increases > 10% (not a cap)
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential landlords in Hoboken renewing a lease with a current tenant
rules.citation: Hoboken Code ch. 158, art. I (Ord. No. B-750, adopted 2025-04-02)
rules.quoted_span: All residential landlords seeking to increase rent by more than 10% upon a renewal of a lease with a current tenant year over year shall be required to make the following disclosures to existing tenants
rules.conflict_note: Categorisation: a disclosure duty recorded under rent_increase_limits. Decided by Hamza 2026-10-04 (L095, Q15): added with conflict_flag true.

rules.title: Rent Control – Newark Code Title XIX, § 19:2-3.1
rules.requirement: For multiple dwellings subject to Newark rent control, the annual rent increase at lease expiry may not exceed the CPI change (15 months to 3 months before the increase) and in no case 4%; increases require substantial code compliance and registration.
rules.key_value: CPI change, capped at 4% per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: Minimum units: 1; All multiple dwellings (buildings with one or more rented apartments) except the listed exemptions
rules.exemptions: Public housing; transient hotels/motels; commercial space; newly constructed multiple dwellings (exempt for the initial-mortgage amortisation period or 30 years, whichever less) and vacant dwellings under §§ 19:2-18.1/18.2; federally/state rehabilitated Section 8 units; units under government rent regulation contracts
rules.citation: Newark Code § 19:2-3.1 (Ord. 6 PSF-A(S), 9-5-2017; amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I)
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.

rules.title: No just cause eviction rule at city level
rules.requirement: Newark has no local just-cause ordinance; the state Anti-Eviction Act (NJ-JUST-01) governs.

rules.title: No security deposits rule at city level
rules.requirement: No Newark deposit ordinance; N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 (NJ-DEP-01) governs.

rules.title: No application screening fees rule at city level
rules.requirement: No Newark application-fee ordinance; N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1 (NJ-FEE-01) governs.

rules.title: Ban the Box – housing (criminal record check practices) – Newark Code Title II, ch. 2:31, art. 1
rules.requirement: In connection with any rental, a Newark landlord or broker may not inquire into criminal history before determining the applicant otherwise qualified, may consider only limited recent records, and must give notice and an opportunity to present rehabilitation evidence before denying housing on that basis.
rules.key_value: criminal-record inquiry limited to post-qualification stage; individualised review
rules.coverage_conditions: Rentals of real property in Newark except owner-occupied two-family dwellings and rooms in owner-occupied one-family homes
rules.exemptions: A single apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rooms rented by the owner-occupant of a one-family dwelling; properties in government programmes for individuals with criminal histories
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or real estate broker may hold a housing unit open until an applicant provides information about rehabilitation, but a landlord or real estate broker is not required to hold a housing unit after making an initial determination of an applicant's eligibility.

rules.title: No algorithmic rent setting rule at city level
rules.requirement: Newark has no local algorithmic rent-setting ordinance; the state FAIR Act (NJ-ALG-01, not yet effective) is the only rule. Change test T2 requires that neither the Hoboken nor the Jersey City ban applies to Newark addresses.
rules.citation: none (NJ FAIR Act P.L.2026 c.43 from 2027-07-01)

rules.title: No rent increase limits rule at city level
rules.requirement: Boston may not enact rent control (M.G.L. c.40P, § 4); its 2023 home-rule petition H.3744 was sent to study on 2024-09-09 (see BOS-RENT-P1). No rent cap applies to Boston addresses.
rules.citation: M.G.L. c.40P, § 4; Mass. H.3744 (193rd) – study order
rules.quoted_span: that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections

rules.title: H.3744 – Boston home-rule petition for rent stabilization and eviction protections (died in study)
rules.requirement: Boston's 2023 home-rule petition asking the Legislature to authorise rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections was accompanied by a study order on 2024-09-09 at the end of the 193rd General Court and never became law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would have applied to Boston if enacted; never in force
rules.citation: Mass. H.3744 (193rd General Court) – study order H.5035 (2024-09-09)
rules.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act (notice of tenants' rights on termination) – Boston Ordinance (2020) [notice-only]
rules.requirement: Any landlord ending a Boston tenancy (notice to quit or non-renewal) must give the tenant the City's Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time and file a copy with the Office of Housing Stability; it does not itself require just cause.
rules.key_value: notice-of-rights duty on termination (no just-cause requirement)
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords in Boston ending a tenancy; foreclosing owners
rules.citation: Boston Code of Ordinances ch. 9, § 9-20 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
rules.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act requires any landlord to provide renters with a Notice of Tenant’s Rights and Resources when planning to end a tenancy agreement.
rules.conflict_note: Decided by Hamza 2026-10-04 (Q5): recorded as a just_cause_eviction rule, notice-only (no just-cause requirement); conflict_flag retained to signal the categorisation choice.

rules.title: No security deposits rule at city level
rules.requirement: No Boston deposit ordinance; M.G.L. c.186, § 15B (MA-DEP-01) governs.

rules.title: No application screening fees rule at city level
rules.requirement: No Boston application-fee ordinance; M.G.L. c.186, § 15B (MA-FEE-01) governs.

rules.title: Boston Fair Housing Commission – rental assistance / Section 8 protection (Boston Fair Housing Ordinance and regulations)
rules.requirement: In the City of Boston it is illegal to discriminate in renting housing on the basis of protected classes that include rental assistance (e.g., renters using Section 8 vouchers); the Boston Fair Housing Commission enforces these local, state and federal protections.
rules.key_value: rental assistance / Section 8 voucher use is a protected class locally
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing in the City of Boston
rules.citation: Boston Fair Housing Commission regulations (Boston Code ch. 10, § 10-3 Fair Housing Ordinance – section not verified)
rules.quoted_span: In the City of Boston, it’s illegal to discriminate when renting, buying, selling, or securing financing for any housing.

rules.title: No algorithmic rent setting rule at city level
rules.requirement: Boston has no local algorithmic rent-setting ordinance; the only Massachusetts measures are the pending state bills S.2983/H.5222 (MA-ALG-P1/P2).

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND-funded and IDP housing) – Feb 2017
rules.requirement: Housing providers that receive Department of Neighborhood Development funding or land, or have income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy, may not impose blanket criminal-history bans and must disregard non-convictions, sealed/expunged records, juvenile records and convictions over five years old, assessing applicants case by case.
rules.key_value: no blanket criminal-history denials; 5-year look-back (city-funded/IDP housing)
rules.coverage_conditions: City-funded housing only: providers receiving DND funding/land or with BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy units
rules.exemptions: Market-rate housing without DND funding or IDP units; where federal/state law imposes a conflicting criminal-history requirement
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, February 2017) – policy, not ordinance
rules.quoted_span:
Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or 
land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development 
Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies 
housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions.
rules.conflict_note: Policy (not legislation) with city-funded scope; Decided by Hamza 2026-10-04 (L088): recorded as BOS-SCRN-02, scope city-funded only, conflict_flag true, low confidence.

rules.title: No rent increase limits rule at city level
rules.requirement: Cambridge may not enact rent control (M.G.L. c.40P, § 4); no rent cap applies to Cambridge addresses (T5).
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind

rules.title: Tenants' Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance – Cambridge Mun. Code ch. 8.71 [notice-only]
rules.requirement: Cambridge landlords must give every tenant the City's Tenants' Rights and Resources guide at the start of a tenancy and again when taking legal steps to terminate it (e.g., notice to quit); it does not itself require just cause. Violations: $300 per day.
rules.key_value: notice-of-rights duty at tenancy start and termination (no just-cause requirement)
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Cambridge, including single units
rules.exemptions: Rental units in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, short-term substance-abuse treatment facilities; short-term rental units under Zoning § 4.60
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance requires owners, landlords, and management companies to provide you with information at the start of your lease or tenancy as well as when your tenancy is being terminated.
rules.conflict_note: Decided by Hamza 2026-10-04 (Q5): recorded as a just_cause_eviction rule, notice-only (no just-cause requirement); conflict_flag retained to signal the categorisation choice.

rules.title: No security deposits rule at city level
rules.requirement: No Cambridge deposit ordinance; M.G.L. c.186, § 15B (MA-DEP-01) governs.

rules.title: No application screening fees rule at city level
rules.requirement: No Cambridge application-fee ordinance; M.G.L. c.186, § 15B (MA-FEE-01) governs.

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance – source of income protection – Cambridge Mun. Code ch. 14.04
rules.requirement: The Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance, enforced by the Cambridge Human Rights Commission, prohibits housing discrimination based on protected categories including source of income (Section 8 and public benefits).
rules.key_value: source of income (incl. Section 8) protected locally
rules.coverage_conditions: Real estate transactions in Cambridge
rules.quoted_span: Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits

rules.title: No algorithmic rent setting rule at city level
rules.requirement: Cambridge has no algorithmic rent-setting ordinance; on 2026-06-22 the City Council passed only a policy order asking the City Manager to draft options. The pending state bills (MA-ALG-P1/P2) are the only measures.
rules.citation: none (policy order June 2026; MA bills pending)
rules.quoted_span: City council also unanimously passed a policy order initiating steps to ban residential property management companies from contracting companies that use algorithmic and AI-driven models to recommend what they should charge for rent.
rules.conflict_note: Negative finding vs pending: Cambridge policy order (June 2026) directs drafting of an ordinance; no ordinance text exists.
